images.caption: Figure 1:Training vision models for weight-space programming.(a)Edit-Ready Training (ERT) simulates edits during training to make vision models better editable by LLMs.(b)Through our WeightLab an LLM agent can iteratively edit a vision model’s weights to change its behavior.(c)ERT improves vision model editability through LLMs, which is indicated by an increased mean net edit score over all nine settings, and the gain of ERT over ERM on the three settings that are hardest (bars: 95% bootstrap confidence;∗:p<0.05p<0.05).

Figure 2:Two image types are used during editing.Supportimages carry the class they should receive after the edit (concept to relabel, errors to correct).Referenceimages are samples whose predictions must stay as they are.

Figure 3:Edit locations.Edits changing only the weights of the final layer, its weights and bias, the backbone (alone or with the final layer), or only the bias or nothing, for thennedit processes of Astra and Opus behindTab.1, in total and split by training method, task and backbone.

Figure 5:Progress per edit.Net score (upper curves) and change in test accuracy (lower curves, as a fraction) after each of the 8 edit calls, averaged over the nine settings and all edit processes ofTab.1. Bands show±1\pm 1standard error.

images.caption: Figure 8:Head changes of all main-table edits, by backbone.One row per edit process, grouped by editor and, within an editor, by the training method of the edited network (left strip). Horizontal axis: the edited head units, from the largest to the smallest change (rank, log scale, the same in all panels; the head has 512 units in ResNet-18, 2,048 in ResNet-50 and 768 in ViT-B/16). Color: size of the change of the unit (log scale). Rows without color changed no head weight. Right strip: the edit also changed a tensor outside the head.
